headline: GLM 5.2 beats Claude in cybersecurity benchmarks
summary: An open-weight LLM from Zhipu AI achieved a 39% F1 score, outperforming Claude Opus in detecting Insecure Direct Object References.
details: GLM 5.2, an open-weight model from Zhipu AI, has surpassed Claude Opus in detecting Insecure Direct Object References (IDORs), achieving a 39% F1 score on Semgrep's benchmark. This marks a significant step for open-weight models in complex security tasks.

The benchmark used the same dataset and prompt as previous evaluations of frontier coding agents. GLM 5.2's performance was particularly surprising as it was tested without the extensive scaffolding used by Semgrep's own multimodal pipeline, which achieved a higher 53-61% F1 score.

Semgrep's multimodal pipeline, designed for static analysis, utilizes a purpose-built harness that enumerates application endpoints and guides the AI model. This contrasts with GLM 5.2's evaluation, which used a simpler Pydantic AI harness with basic guidance, demonstrating the model's inherent capability.

GLM 5.2 was released on June 13, 2026, with open weights and release notes following on June 16. Its MIT license allows for inspection, fine-tuning, and self-hosted deployment, which is crucial for security teams handling sensitive data.
